label: prop:tetrahedral-hbond-directions
title: The four H-bond directions are tetrahedral ($\cos\theta_0 = -1/3$)
html:
The four hydrogen-bond directions of a water in ice — two donor, two acceptor — point to the vertices of a regular tetrahedron. Taking the vertex vectors (\pm 1, \pm 1, \pm 1) with an even number of minus signs, they sum to zero, each has squared length 3, and any two have dot product -1. The bond-angle cosine is

 \cos\theta_0 \;=\; \frac{u_i \cdot u_j}{|u_i|\,|u_j|} \;=\; \frac{-1}{3}, \qquad \theta_0 = \arccos\!\left(-\tfrac13\right) \approx 109.47^\circ.

This is the symmetric reference angle \theta_0 from which oxygen's lone pairs displace the H–O–H angle to \approx 104.5^\circ (the quadratic-well shift). The four facts — balanced sum, squared length 3, pairwise dot -1, and \cos\theta_0 = -1/3 — hold exactly over \mathbb{R}.
heading: Proposition
